Work-to-live people are not necessarily lazy, but they do have better things to do with their time and money than work.

The verb "to enjoy" is a little different from its equivalent "to like", "to love". "To enjoy", as used here, suggests that there are specific things or activities that we particularly like to do, that we take special delight or satisfaction in. So we say: I really enjoy reading, I enjoy gardening, I enjoy going to the theatre. But we do not usually say: I enjoy the rain, or I enjoy my neighbour's barking dog
